- **self**: Stop placement vs liquidation buffer (4/3)

## How it works

- [statement] A stop set inside normal short-term price noise can be triggered and fill badly. SEC staff: a stop 'may be triggered by a short-term, intraday price move that results in an execution price for the stop order that is substantially worse', and brokers differ on whether last-sale or quotation prices trigger it. Hyperliquid builds its mark price from 'external CEX prices with Hyperliquid's book state', which it says is 'more robust than using a single instantaneous book price'. (medium confidence) — https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-15 · keywords: Stop placement vs liquidation buffer · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A stop price is a trigger, not a guaranteed fill. SEC staff (equities): a stop order becomes a market order at the stop price, and its execution price 'can deviate significantly from the stop price due to the prices of available liquidity'; a stop-limit 'may not be executed if the stock's price moves away from the specified limit price'. The same failure shows on perps: Hyperliquid's FAQ says a long stop-loss with a $10 limit 'may rest at $10 without filling' if price drops from $11 to $9, and Mudrex says a skipped stop-limit can leave the position to be liquidated. (high confidence) — https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-15 · keywords: Stop placement vs liquidation buffer · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/support/faq/trade-outcome-looks-incorrect/my-tp-sl-did-not-execute-correctly, https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/take-profit-and-stop-loss-orders-tp-sl, https://mudrex.com/learn/why-crypto-futures-liquidated-despite-stop-loss/
- [statement] Hyperliquid's default slippage tolerance for market TP/SL orders is 10%. The limit price on a TP/SL order sets the slippage bound instead: a more aggressive limit makes a fill more likely but allows more slippage. In the docs' example, a long stop-loss triggered at $10 with a $10 limit may rest unfilled if price gaps down, while an $8 limit would likely fill between $9 and $8. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/take-profit-and-stop-loss-orders-tp-sl · keywords: Stop placement vs liquidation buffer · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/support/faq/trade-outcome-looks-incorrect/my-tp-sl-did-not-execute-correctly
- [statement] Pick the stop first, size from it, and treat leverage as an output. Kraken's sizing guide uses position size = (account value x risk %) / |entry - stop|, identical for shorts (stop above entry); leverage 'doesn't change the dollar risk if the stop is hit', and 'Never let your leverage setting determine how large a position you open'. Wealthsimple: 'The maximum leverage a platform allows is a limit, not a recommendation.' (medium confidence) — https://www.kraken.com/learn/futures-trading-position-sizing-leverage · keywords: Stop placement vs liquidation buffer · also: https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/learn/avoid-liquidation-perpetual-futures
